title: Japan Raises Interest Rates to 31-Year High to Fight Rising Prices
subtitle: The Bank of Japan moves to control inflation as global economic uncertainty continues.

summary.en: Japan’s central bank has increased its main interest rate to 1.25%, reaching its highest level since 1995. This decision is part of a global effort to stop inflation caused by the ongoing conflict in Iran. Governor Kazuo Ueda stated that future rate changes will depend on careful analysis of economic data. While the move aims to stabilize the economy, some board members disagreed with the decision. Investors are now watching closely to see if further increases will happen before the end of the year.
summary.zh: 日本中央銀行已將主要利率調升至百分之一點二五，達到一九九五年以來最高水準。此決策是全球抑制伊朗衝突所引發通膨努力的一部分。總裁植田和男表示，未來的利率調整將取決於對經濟數據的審慎分析。儘管此舉旨在穩定經濟，但部分委員會成員對該決策持保留意見。投資人目前正密切關注年底前是否會進一步升息。

paragraphs.en: Japan’s central bank has taken a major step to manage the country's economy by raising interest rates to a 31-year high. The Bank of Japan (BoJ) decided to increase its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%. This is the highest level the rate has reached since 1995. This decision is part of a broader trend, as central banks around the world work to control inflation—the general increase in prices for goods and services—which has been made worse by the ongoing war in Iran.
paragraphs.zh: 日本中央銀行採取了重大舉措來管理國家經濟，將利率調升至三十一年來的新高。日本銀行（Bank of Japan）決定將目標利率從百分之一調升至百分之一點二五。這是自一九九五年以來該利率達到的最高水準。此項決策是全球趨勢的一部分，各國央行正致力於控制通貨膨脹——即商品與服務價格的普遍上漲——而伊朗持續進行的戰爭加劇了此一問題。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the decision to raise rates was not supported by everyone on the BoJ’s nine-member policy committee. Two members voted against the increase, showing that there is still debate among officials about how quickly the bank should act. Kazuo Ueda, the governor of the Bank of Japan, explained that the bank is now focused on keeping inflation at its target of 2%. In August, Japan’s inflation rate was 1.9%, which is very close to that goal. Ueda noted that if inflation goes too far above this target, it could hurt the Japanese economy.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，日本銀行九人政策委員會中並非所有成員都支持升息決策。有兩名成員投票反對，顯示官員對於銀行應採取多快的行動仍存在分歧。日本銀行總裁植田和男（Kazuo Ueda）解釋，銀行目前專注於將通膨率維持在百分之二的目標。八月份日本的通膨率為百分之一點九，非常接近該目標。植田指出，若通膨率過度高於此目標，可能會損害日本經濟。

paragraphs.en: This move follows a period of significant pressure on the Japanese currency, the yen. Throughout this year, the yen has become weaker compared to the US dollar. A weaker currency can make imports more expensive, which adds to the problem of rising prices for consumers. To help fix this, the US and Japan worked together in late July to support the value of the yen. The US Treasury even moved to sell at least $10 billion in euros to buy yen, an action taken to stop the currency from falling to a 40-year low.
paragraphs.zh: 此舉是在日本貨幣「日圓」面臨巨大壓力的一段時期後所做出的。今年以來，日圓相對於美元持續走弱。貨幣貶值會導致進口成本增加，進而加劇消費者面臨的物價上漲問題。為了協助解決此問題，美國與日本於七月下旬合作以支撐日圓匯率。美國財政部甚至採取行動，拋售至少一百億美元的歐元以買入日圓，此舉旨在阻止日圓跌至四十年來的最低點。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the path for future interest rate changes remains uncertain. Governor Ueda said that the bank does not have a set plan for when the next increase might happen. He emphasized that the committee will look at new data carefully before making any more moves. “We are at a phase where we need to look at various data carefully,” Ueda said. He added that the bank must take timely action as needed, but he did not rule out the possibility of more rate increases in the future if economic conditions require them.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，利率調整的後續路徑仍不明朗。植田總裁表示，銀行對於下次升息的時間點並無既定計畫。他強調，委員會在採取進一步行動前，將會審慎檢視最新數據。植田表示：「我們正處於需要仔細觀察各項數據的階段。」他補充說，銀行必須視情況採取及時行動，但也不排除若經濟情勢需要，未來可能進一步升息的可能性。

paragraphs.en: Other major central banks are also dealing with similar challenges. The US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank have both tightened their monetary policy—a process where a central bank manages the amount of money in the economy to influence interest rates and control inflation—this month. Meanwhile, the Bank of England has decided to keep its interest rates steady at 3.75% for now, though it warned that future increases might be necessary because of the fallout from the conflict in Iran.
paragraphs.zh: 其他主要央行也面臨類似挑戰。美國聯準會（Federal Reserve）與歐洲中央銀行（European Central Bank）本月皆緊縮了貨幣政策——即央行透過管理經濟中的貨幣總量來影響利率並控制通膨的過程。與此同時，英國央行（Bank of England）決定暫時將利率維持在百分之三點七五，但警告由於伊朗衝突帶來的後續影響，未來可能仍有升息必要。

paragraphs.en: Experts are now watching the Bank of Japan to see what happens next. Fred Neumann, the chief Asia economist at HSBC, noted that the split vote among the board members suggests that the bank will likely remain cautious. While many investors do not expect back-to-back rate hikes, they are looking for signs that officials might be ready to raise rates again in December. The recent change in policy has already had an impact on the stock market, with the Nikkei stock market index rising nearly 2% following the news.
paragraphs.zh: 專家們正密切觀察日本銀行的後續動向。匯豐銀行（HSBC）亞洲首席經濟學家紐曼（Fred Neumann）指出，委員會成員間的投票分歧顯示銀行可能會保持謹慎。雖然許多投資人並不預期會連續升息，但他們正尋找官員可能準備在十二月再次升息的跡象。這項政策變動已對股市產生影響，日經股價指數（Nikkei）在消息公布後上漲了近百分之二。

paragraphs.en: For now, the Bank of Japan is trying to balance the need to keep inflation stable with the need to support the economy. The shift in focus from trying to boost inflation to ensuring it does not become too high marks a significant change in the bank’s strategy. As the global economy continues to face challenges from the conflict in the Middle East, the actions of central banks like the BoJ will remain a key factor for businesses and consumers alike. Whether the bank decides to raise rates again soon will depend on how the economy performs in the coming months.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，日本銀行正試圖在維持通膨穩定與支撐經濟之間取得平衡。從試圖刺激通膨轉向確保通膨不會過高，標誌著該銀行策略的重大轉變。隨著全球經濟持續面臨中東衝突帶來的挑戰，像日本銀行這類央行的行動，對企業與消費者而言仍是關鍵因素。銀行是否決定在近期再次升息，將取決於未來幾個月的經濟表現。

quiz.question: What specific action did the US Treasury take to assist the Japanese yen in late July?

options.A: They increased their own interest rates to match Japan's.
options.B: They sold a significant amount of euros to purchase yen.
options.C: They pressured the Bank of Japan to raise rates to a 31-year high.
options.D: They stopped importing goods from Japan to stabilize the currency.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，美國財政部為了防止日圓匯率跌至 40 年新低，採取了賣出至少 100 億歐元來買進日圓的行動。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提到美國為了日圓而調整自身利率；選項 C 錯誤，此舉是兩國合作而非美國單方面施壓；選項 D 則完全未在文中提及。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the Bank of Japan be hesitant to raise interest rates again immediately?

options.A: Because inflation has already dropped well below the 2% target.
options.B: Because the Japanese stock market has crashed following the recent rate hike.
options.C: Because there is a lack of consensus among the bank's policy committee members.
options.D: Because the US Federal Reserve has requested that Japan keep rates steady.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。第二段提到九人委員會中有兩人反對升息，顯示內部意見分歧；第六段專家 Fred Neumann 也指出，這種分裂的投票結果暗示央行將保持謹慎。選項 A 錯誤，目前通膨 1.9% 極接近 2% 目標；選項 B 錯誤，文中提到日經指數反而上漲了近 2%；選項 D 錯誤，文中未提及美國聯準會要求日本維持利率。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'fallout' mean in the context of the conflict in Iran?

options.A: The physical destruction caused by weapons.
options.B: The negative side effects or consequences.
options.C: The sudden end of a political agreement.
options.D: The radioactive dust released after an explosion.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「fallout」並非指核輻射塵，而是指某個事件（如戰爭）所帶來的「負面後果」或「餘波」。文章提到英國央行因伊朗衝突的餘波而預警未來可能需升息。選項 A 太過狹隘；選項 C 與 D 均不符合經濟新聞的語境，屬於對單字的錯誤解讀。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of this article regarding the Bank of Japan?

options.A: Explaining the history of Japanese interest rates since 1995.
options.B: Describing the military impact of the conflict in Iran on global trade.
options.C: Analyzing the effectiveness of the US Treasury's intervention in currency markets.
options.D: Discussing the BoJ's strategic shift to manage inflation through interest rate adjustments.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心在於日本央行如何透過調整利率來應對通膨與經濟挑戰，並提到其策略從過去的「刺激通膨」轉向「穩定通膨」。選項 A 只是背景資訊；選項 B 是導致經濟問題的原因之一，而非主旨；選項 C 僅是文章第三段提到的局部細節，無法涵蓋全文。
